html:
The Cheras were one of the three crowned Tamil dynasties of south India, ruling the western coast in today's Kerala and the Kongu country inland. On the 500 and 700 maps they hold the far south west.

The early Cheras appear in the edicts of Ashoka as the Keralaputras and in Tamil Sangam poems as patrons of bards. Their wealth came from the coast. Ports such as Muziris sent black pepper, pearls and fine cloth to Roman and Arab traders. Their main inland city was Karur.

The centuries around 500 and 700 are dim. Much of the Tamil country fell under the Kalabhras, and little is known of the Cheras in these years. A later line, the Chera Perumals of Makotai, ruled from about 800 to the early 1100s, often at war with the Pandyas and the Cholas. Kerala then broke into smaller kingdoms, such as Calicut and Cochin.
sum: The Cheras were one of the three crowned Tamil dynasties of south India, ruling the western coast in today's Kerala and the Kongu country inland. On the 500 and 700 maps they hold the far south west.
